findings.title: Security Advisory: Please Lock Down Your Administrator Access
findings.summary_md: The Sangoma FreePBX security team opened this advisory thread on August 26, 2025 after exploitation of internet-exposed administrator panels was detected, shipping an EDGE endpoint fix the same day and the stable fix on August 28. It publishes the infection checklist still referenced months later: POST requests to modular.php in Apache access logs reaching back to August 21, the leftover /var/www/html/.clean.sh file, calls to extension 9998 in Asterisk logs, unknown rows in the ampusers table, and restricting the Administrator Control Panel with the Firewall module.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass Leading to SQL Injection and RCE (GHSA-m42g-xg4c-5f3h, CVE-2025-57819)
findings.summary_md: The official FreePBX advisory for CVE-2025-57819, published August 28, 2025: insufficiently sanitized user-supplied input in the commercial endpoint module allows unauthenticated access to the FreePBX Administrator, arbitrary database manipulation, and remote code execution across FreePBX 15, 16, and 17, patched in endpoint 15.0.66, 16.0.89, and 17.0.3. The vendor states attacks began on or before August 21, 2025 against systems with the admin panel exposed to the internet, scoring the flaw Critical 10.0 under CVSS v4.

findings.title: watchTowr-vs-FreePBX-CVE-2025-57819 (public PoC and detection artifact generator)
findings.summary_md: watchTowr Labs published a working exploit for CVE-2025-57819 on September 8, 2025, chaining the auth bypass through SQL injection to webshell upload and root-level access, with a fallback that adds a rogue administrator user. Public weaponization one week after the vendor fix matters for this story because the JOMANGY webshell cleanup routine deletes files matching *-watchTowr-*.php, tying the campaign to artifacts from this exact release.

findings.title: Authenticated Command Injection in FreePBX Administration GUI (GHSA-vm9p-46mv-5xvw, CVE-2025-64328)
findings.summary_md: FreePBX's advisory for CVE-2025-64328, published November 5, 2025: a post-authentication command injection in the filestore module's testconnection check_ssh_connect() function, introduced around March 2025, affecting filestore 17.0.2.36 through versions below 17.0.3 and fixed in 17.0.3. An authenticated administrator-panel user can execute arbitrary shell commands as the asterisk user. CVSS v4.0 base score 8.6 High.

findings.title: Unveiling the Weaponized Web Shell EncystPHP
findings.summary_md: FortiGuard Labs documents EncystPHP, a persistent FreePBX webshell delivered via CVE-2025-64328 in incidents starting early December 2025, and attributes the activity to INJ3CTOR3, an actor targeting VoIP infrastructure since 2019 via CVE-2019-19006 and later CVE-2021-45461. The report details the newfpbx UID-0 backdoor account, crontab entries re-downloading k.php droppers at one to three minute intervals, webshell copies masquerading as ajax.php across /var/www/html subdirectories, and dropper infrastructure at 45.234.176.202 and 187.108.1.130.

findings.title: Scans for EncystPHP Webshell (SANS ISC diary 32892)
findings.summary_md: SANS ISC recorded live scanning for the EncystPHP webshell on FreePBX systems on April 13, 2026: GET requests to /admin/modules/phones/ajax.php carrying the webshell's hardcoded md5 credential, and /restapps/applications.php exploit requests that download k.php from 45.95.147.178 and reset passwords on ten accounts including root, asterisk, and freepbxuser. The probes originated from 160.119.76.250 in the Netherlands, which also swept for other FreePBX vulnerabilities.

findings.title: JOMANGY: INJ3CTOR3's Self-Healing FreePBX Toll Fraud Campaign
findings.summary_md: Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs' original disclosure, one day before the Cyberpress coverage in this story: a multi-stage Bash dropper deploys the previously undocumented JOMANGY PHP webshell with six mutually protecting persistence channels, 18 backdoor accounts of which nine are UID-0, and live toll fraud code routing calls through the victim's SIP trunks. The report assesses CVE-2025-57819 and CVE-2025-64328 as the likely entry vectors, catalogs a 3,080-IP C2 inventory in people2.txt with roughly 39 percent on Alibaba Cloud, and documents eviction of 50-plus rival webshell signatures and blocking of 11 competitor C2 IPs.
